analysis: Examined test-only changes. CoordinatorClientTests.swift head 578-591 replaces sampled nextDelay() bounds checks with deterministic nextDelayRange() equality (0.5...1, 1...2, 2...4, 2...4, reset to 0.5...1); no security behavior. CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift head 10-12/21 updates comments saying the suite now runs in provider CI rather than being skipped. Head 456-491 adds tests asserting that a coordinator-side 1012 (service restart) close reconnects within 1.5 s, and that a session open past a configurable stableSessionDuration resets backoff. Head 652-726 adds a reconnectPolicy parameter to makeClient/CoordinatorClient and helpers. These tests imply production changes outside this batch: a CoordinatorReconnectPolicy type, a new CoordinatorClient init parameter, nextDelayRange(), and special-case fast reconnect on close code 1012. Integration should verify in production source (CoordinatorClient reconnect loop): (1) a malicious or MITM-free but compromised coordinator path cannot weaponize 1012 to cause tight reconnect loops; repeated 1012 should not bypass backoff indefinitely (availability, TB-002, A-018); a 0-1 s wait per 1012 seems bounded, but confirm repeated 1012 closes still grow or rate-limit, so the provider does not hammer the coordinator during real failover (thundering herd across fleet). (2) Each reconnect still re-signs a fresh attestation blob (TB-009, coordinatorRegistrationRegeneratesAttestationOnReconnect) and does not reuse endpoint-resumption/App Attest state improperly (T-053, TB-011). (3) stableSessionDuration default (comment implies 60 s) is not configurable by untrusted input. The coordinator is trusted, so close codes come from a trusted party; no regression is evidenced in these test units.
